training-data.name: Training Data
training-data.bio: Podcast: OpenAI's Greg Brockman: Why Human Attention Is the New Bottleneck

html_en:
As AI models grow increasingly powerful, a fascinating paradox emerges: the industry's brightest minds are simultaneously celebrating breakthroughs while grappling with fundamental questions about buildable, sustainable businesses in an era of rapidly advancing intelligence.

The Intelligence Ceiling Debate

Sam Altman's candid reflection this week cuts to the heart of AI development priorities.
"i keep thinking i want the models to be cheaper/faster more than i want them to be smarter, but it seems that just being smarter is still the most important thing"
he tweeted, capturing a tension many builders feel. This sentiment comes as Altman also praised GPT-5.5's performance in fast mode, suggesting he'd been "psyoped by twitter on medium for a bit." Meanwhile, OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman offered a striking assessment of where we stand on the path to artificial general intelligence. Speaking on the Training Data podcast, Brockman positioned current models as remarkably capable:
"According to my view of where we are, I think we're about 80% of the way there... They're certainly more capable than I am at writing software."
He shared a compelling anecdote about an internal systems engineer who gave GPT-5.3 a design document before sleeping, only to wake up and find
"the model had actually implemented the initial spec, had seen that it was slow, had added instrumentation, had actually run the code, used a profiler to figure out where things were slow, and iterated multiple times until it had gotten to an optimized result."
Watch: OpenAI's Greg Brockman on Training Data

The Economics of Enhanced Labor

As models approach human-level performance in specific domains, Box CEO Aaron Levie offered a compelling counter-narrative to AI displacement fears. Rather than replacing engineers, he argues AI is creating a "force multiplier effect" that could dramatically expand demand for technical talent.
"Do you continue with your pared down approach, or do you start to hire more engineers because each engineer is 2X or 5X more capable than before? In almost every company I'm talking to, they're doing the latter,"
Levie observed, describing how life sciences companies previously constrained by engineering costs are now expanding their technical ambitions. This perspective finds practical expression in everyday workflows. Peter Yang demonstrated the personal productivity gains possible, describing how he uses Claude for digital organization:
"Tell me what apps load on computer bootup. Give me a plan to clean this up... Help me organize my Google Drive. Let's review your plan first before doing anything."
His files now "spark joy," he noted with characteristic humor.

Infrastructure and Architecture Evolution

Behind the user experience improvements lies a sophisticated rethinking of AI system architecture. Anthropic's engineering team this week detailed their approach to "Scaling Managed Agents," introducing a fundamental shift in how long-running AI systems are designed. The key insight centers on what they call "decoupling the brain from the hands." Rather than bundling agent logic, execution environments, and session management into monolithic containers, Anthropic has virtualized each component. As they explain in their engineering blog post:
"We virtualized the components of an agent: a session (the append-only log of everything that happened), a harness (the loop that calls Claude and routes Claude's tool calls to the relevant infrastructure), and a sandbox (an execution environment where Claude can run code and edit files)."
This architectural philosophy echoes operating system design principles, creating abstractions stable enough for "programs as yet unthought of." The approach solves practical problems too—when containers fail, sessions survive, and new containers can be spun up seamlessly. Meanwhile, PSPDFKit's Peter Steinberger shipped Crabbox 0.3.0, highlighting the rapid iteration happening in developer tooling.
"🦀 Crabbox 0.3.0 is out. Remote Linux runs for dirty worktrees"
he announced, adding features like GitHub browser login and durable run events.

Market Reality Check

Not every AI venture is thriving in this environment of rapid advancement. At AI Engineers Europe, a sobering moment came when Swyx witnessed a founder shut down their company live on stage. Vibe-kanban, despite maintaining 30,000 monthly active users, couldn't find sustainable revenue. The founder's post-mortem was stark:
"Everyone who is making money is doing 2 things: selling to enterprise, and reselling tokens. We were doing neither,"
as Swyx reported. The project lives on as open source, but the shutdown illustrates the challenging unit economics facing consumer AI applications. This reality check resonates with broader venture concerns. Investor Nikunj expressed frustration with current funding dynamics:
"Too many funds are capping downside right now, instead of maximizing upside... 'well at least big token factory will acquire them so our downside is capped'"
he tweeted, arguing this approach won't generate the returns needed for successful venture funds.

The New Workflow Paradigm

Perhaps most tellingly, Dan Shipper captured what may be the emerging standard for knowledge work:
"clear that this is how we'll be doing most of our work for the next 10 years: agent running continuously on the left, application that you + the agent use on the right"
he observed, sharing a screenshot that felt both futuristic and oddly familiar. This vision of human-AI collaboration—continuous, contextual, and increasingly seamless—suggests we're moving beyond the current paradigm of prompt-and-response toward something more akin to persistent digital assistants. The question isn't whether this future will arrive, but how quickly the infrastructure, business models, and human workflows can adapt to support it.
html_zh:
今日AI社区迎来了一系列关于构建真正有用产品与技术可行性之间紧张关系的深刻洞察，同时AI智能体开始从实验走向生产环境。

企业现实与技术乐观主义的碰撞

在本周的AI工程大会上，一个令人深思的时刻出现了：@tokengobbler在台上宣布关闭了拥有3万月活用户的Vibe-kanban项目。正如@swyx转述的那样：
"每个赚钱的人都在做两件事：向企业销售，和转售token。我们两个都没做。"
这种坦率揭示了AI创业公司面临的严峻现实。尽管拥有相当可观的用户基础，但缺乏可持续的收入模式最终导致了项目的终结。 Box首席执行官Aaron Levie提供了另一个视角，他认为AI实际上会增加而不是取代对软件工程师的需求：
想象一下你是一家生命科学公司。10年前你想大力投资实验室自动化，大规模处理数据和其他软件。你发现成本太高，无法与科技公司竞争那么多工程师...现在，AI出现了。突然间你拥有了与世界顶级科技公司*完全相同*的输出token。
这种观点暗示，AI可能会民主化工程能力，使非科技公司能够进行以前无法承受的软件项目。

智能体技术的生产化突破

Anthropic通过发布托管智能体服务，在将AI智能体从实验推向生产环境方面迈出了重要一步。他们的关键洞察是将智能体架构虚拟化：
我们将智能体的组件虚拟化：会话（所有发生事件的仅追加日志），工具（调用Claude并将Claude的工具调用路由到相关基础设施的循环），以及沙箱（Claude可以运行代码和编辑文件的执行环境）。
这种"将大脑与双手解耦"的方法解决了智能体部署中的一个根本问题：如何构建既强大又可维护的系统。 与此同时，Dan Shipper描绘了他对未来工作流程的愿景：
很明显，这就是我们在未来10年大部分时间的工作方式：左边是持续运行的智能体，右边是你和智能体使用的应用程序

OpenAI深度访谈：计算渴望与智能进展

在最近的Training Data播客中，OpenAI联合创始人Greg Brockman提供了公司战略的内部视角。关于计算需求，他的回应令人印象深刻：
在很多方面，我们的业务非常简单。我们购买、租用、构建计算，然后以利润出售。就是这样。只要利润是正的，那么你就想扩大规模，因为解决问题的需求，对智能的需求是无限的。
当被问及是否有足够的计算资源时，他坦率地说：
"没有。真的？是的，绝对没有。"
关于AGI的进展，Brockman表示他们已经完成了80%的路程，并分享了一个令人印象深刻的例子：
我的一位系统工程师...将一份非常复杂的系统优化设计文档交给了模型，然后去睡觉，打算第二天将其分配给他的团队工作一周。当他醒来时，工作已经完成了，模型不仅实现了初始规范，发现它很慢，添加了仪器，实际运行了代码，使用性能分析器找出慢的地方，并迭代多次直到获得了优化结果。
Sam Altman也在推特上透露了他对模型发展的思考：
我一直认为我更希望模型更便宜/更快，而不是更聪明，但似乎仅仅是更聪明仍然是最重要的事情

个人生产力的AI化改造

Peter Yang分享了使用AI进行个人文件管理的创新方法：
让Codex或Claude Code来"断舍离"你的本地文件和Google Drive非常令人满意。我给这些应用完全访问我的计算机和gws（google workspace cli），然后提示诸如："告诉我启动时加载哪些应用。给我一个清理计划。"
他强调总是先要求制定计划，因为这些是半危险的操作。 同时，@steipete发布了Crabbox 0.3.0，为开发者带来了新的远程Linux运行能力和GitHub浏览器登录功能。

投资视角：超越安全下行保护

风险投资人Nikunj对当前投资环境表达了担忧：
太多基金现在都在限制下行风险，而不是最大化上行空间...当我问GP/合伙人为什么做这笔交易时，经过第五次追问，真正的原因出现了，即"至少大型token工厂会收购他们，所以我们的下行风险有限"
这种观察突出了AI繁荣期间投资策略可能发生的微妙但重要的转变，其中安全性可能开始胜过真正的创新潜力。 随着AI智能体从概念验证发展到生产系统，行业正在学习如何在技术可行性、商业可行性和用户需求之间取得平衡。今天的讨论表明，虽然技术能力继续快速发展，但构建可持续AI业务的挑战依然复杂且微妙。
